_scope: External experimental anchors for qm_thermo/external_reference.py. Nothing here is fitted, and no correction may use the scored reaction's own experimental value. Reconstructed 2026-08-04 after the original file was lost; the redox and pyrophosphorylase entries reproduce the published 19.4 kJ/mol referenced column.

redox_couple_equalization.citation: Standard biochemical reduction potentials, pH 7, 298.15 K (Alberty, Thermodynamics of Biochemical Reactions, 2003)
redox_couple_equalization.note: Hydride addition to the nicotinamide ring is electronically identical for NAD and NADP; the 2'-phosphate is a distal spectator. The composite nevertheless puts the two couples 43 kJ/mol apart, and the NADP member is the accurate one. Transfer its QM value with the small tabulated E0' offset.

redox_couple_equalization.citation: Standard biochemical reduction potentials, pH 7, 298.15 K (Alberty, Thermodynamics of Biochemical Reactions, 2003)
redox_couple_equalization.note: Reverse-direction counterpart of rxn00070; direction_sign flips the E0' offset.

isodesmic.reference_name: UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase (EC 2.7.7.9): UTP + alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate = UDP-glucose + PPi
isodesmic.experimental_note: Pyrophosphate is a shared product of the reference and both targets, so it cancels exactly and the residual swap is charge-balanced. This is the condition under which isodesmic referencing works; see the glycosyl note below for the case where it does not.

isodesmic.reference_name: sucrose phosphorylase (EC 2.4.1.7), written in reverse: D-fructose + alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate = phosphate + sucrose
isodesmic.citation: TECRDB, EC 2.7.4.1/2.4.1.7 sucrose phosphorylase, 5 measurements; ModelSEED rxn00577 reversed (measured -7.551 kJ/mol forward)
isodesmic.experimental_note: Written in reverse so that fructose and sucrose cancel between target and reference, leaving the charge-balanced residual UDP-glucose + Pi = UDP + G1P (-4 on both sides at the pH-7 microspecies charges). Both species removed are suspect: ModelSEED stores fructose as a furanose although free fructose in water is ~70% beta-pyranose, and sucrose carries a double anomeric linkage. Independent check: the reference's QM value computed here (+63.9) matches the reversed value from the separately scored 130-reaction set (+62.9) to ~1 kJ/mol. CAVEAT: the anchor is external to the ten but is itself a member of the 130-reaction set (rxn00577), so it must not be counted as independent when reporting on that set.

speciation_substitution.citation: Methylglyoxal aldehyde hydration in water; the free aldehyde is a minor species (>99% hydrated at the aldehyde carbon)
speciation_substitution.note: ModelSEED scores 2-oxopropanal as the free aldehyde. Replacing it with the explicitly computed gem-diol adds one oxygen and two hydrogens, balanced by consuming one water. Worth only ~8 kJ/mol; the bulk of this reaction's error is not speciation.
